To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
uroplakin II (UP-II) gene is expressed in the majority (39.5%) of transitional cell carcinomas but not in bilharsial-related squamous cell carcinoma.
UP-II is a marker of urothelum-type differentiation, that UP-II gene is not mutated in bladder cancer, and that the urothelial epithelium can differentiate in at least three ways.

(a) UP-II gene is expressed in TCCs but not in bilha- rzial bladder SCCs; (b) UP-II gene expression is not altered in TCCs; and (c ) UP expression in bladder epithelium and in bladder cancer may be regulated by vitamin A deficiency and by mesenchymal signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying bladder epithelial differentiation, and the relationship between urothelial and epidermal differentiation.
the molecular biology of UPs and the role of urothelial dysplasia in bladder cancer.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UP-II gene is expressed in TCC but not in bilhamarial bladder SCC.
the expression of UPs in TCCs is a reflection of urothelial cell differentiation.
the urothelial cells in TCCs and SCCs have the capacity to express the urothelio- or epidermis-type differentiation products, but the glandular-type products are absent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UP-II gene is not mutated in TCC but is expressed in a subset of these tumors.
UP-II gene is expressed in TCC, and not in bilharziasis-related SCC, and that the urothelum can undergo at least 3 pathways of differentiation.
the expression of UP-II gene is associated with urothelism and that it is a useful diagnostic marker for TCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of UPs is not a prerequisite for the formation of TCCC but that the loss of UP expression in TCCC may be associated with the acquisition of invasive properties.
the urothelial differentiation pathway may be a target for cancer chemoprevention and/or treatment.
urothelial cells are capable of expressing a variety of differentiation markers and that the relative expression of these markers is determined by the environment in which they are growing.
